ai.name: OpenAI
ai.hook: OpenAI ships GPT-5.6 as three models and turns ChatGPT into a work superapp.
insights: Three sizes: **Luna** ($1/$6 per 1M tokens), **Terra** ($2.50/$15), **Sol** ($5/$30), all with Feb 2026 knowledge cutoff
New **ChatGPT Work** desktop app merges Codex and ChatGPT, plus **Sites beta** and multi-agent beta
Microsoft calls GPT-5.6 the 'preferred model' for Copilot 365 amid breakup rumors, and Fidji Simo just stepped down from OpenAI's no.2 AGI role
ai.for_you: ChatGPT Work's desktop app merging chat+coding is worth a 20-minute test drive: if it handles PT-language client workflows well, it could replace parts of your agency's current stack faster than you'd build custom tooling.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Biggest model launch of the week, top HN story at 1290pts

ai.name: Anthropic
ai.hook: Anthropic builds a 'Jacobian lens' to watch Claude actually think mid-task.
insights: The tool gives the **clearest interpretability view yet** into concept formation inside large models
Findings range from mundane routing patterns to genuinely unnerving emergent behaviors
Comes alongside Claude **Cowork** expanding to mobile/web as a background-agent teammate product
ai.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, this is research-stage but worth knowing if a PT SMB client ever asks 'can we trust what the AI decided.'
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Rare real interpretability finding, not just a product launch

ai.name: Tencent
ai.hook: Tencent's Hy3 open model runs 2.95x faster natively on both Nvidia and AMD.
insights: 295B MoE with only **21B active parameters**, 192 experts, 256K context
Uses MTP speculative decoding, native vLLM support
Competes closely with GLM-5.2 in the open-weight race, though open models still lag closed frontier on agent benchmarks
ai.for_you: If you ever need a self-hosted model for a cost-sensitive PT SMB client with data residency concerns, Hy3 running efficiently on commodity AMD/Nvidia stacks is a real candidate to test.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only concrete open-weight model release with hard performance numbers today

ai.name: Interconnects (Nathan Lambert)
ai.hook: GLM-5.2 marks a real capability threshold for open agents, not just another release.
insights: Framed as a step-change Lambert has been 'carefully monitoring' rather than routine hype
Companion post argues **banning open-source AI would be a mistake**, co-written for a general audience
Signals the open ecosystem (Zyphra, Cohere, Poolside) is widening, not consolidating
ai.for_you: Worth 10 minutes if you're weighing open vs closed models for agency clients on a budget, the open-agent gap is closing faster than most PT SMB decks assume.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most substantive analysis piece in the AI newsletter stack today

ai.name: Lilian Weng
ai.hook: 35 papers distilled into one framework: 'harness engineering' is the new bottleneck, not raw model IQ.
insights: Concept centers on **the scaffolding around agents** (routing, memory, observability) mattering more than the model itself
Echoed by LangChain's new **Deep Agents** course and open-source project
Simon Willison and Will Depue both independently flag coordination/observability as the current UX ceiling
ai.for_you: This is the actual skill gap in your agency's positioning: PT SMBs don't need a bigger model, they need someone who designs the harness around it, that's your wedge over generic 'AI consultants' selling ChatGPT subscriptions.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Cross-referenced by three independent sources today, a real emerging consensus

ai.name: Craig Mod
ai.hook: Writer rebuilds his own newsletter tooling with AI, cuts $7K/year down to $150.
insights: Replaced Campaign Monitor entirely with a self-built AI tool
Calls this the start of a 'golden age of tool building' where anyone builds software fit to their exact need
Draws a hard line: uses AI to build tools, refuses to use it to actually write
ai.for_you: This is your yoga platform's playbook: instead of paying for a generic course/community SaaS, you could vibe-code the exact tool you need for cheaper and own it outright.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most concrete, replicable build story in today's podcast lineup

build_this.name: GPT-5.6 API (Luna tier)
build_this.what_it_is: Cheapest new GPT-5.6 model at $1/$6 per 1M tokens with 90% cache-read discount.
build_this.why_try_it: Swap Luna into an agency client's existing GPT-5.5 workflow this week and compare output quality against the cost drop, the cache-read discount alone could meaningfully cut your per-client API bill on repetitive SMB tasks like invoice parsing or FAQ bots.

build_this.name: llm-meta-ai plugin
build_this.what_it_is: A plugin for Simon Willison's `llm` CLI tool that lets you run prompts against Meta's new Muse Spark 1.1 model.
build_this.why_try_it: If you already use the `llm` CLI for quick prompt testing, this is a 5-minute install to benchmark Muse Spark 1.1's agentic tool-calling against what you're using now for agency client demos.

tech.name: Fidji Simo
tech.hook: OpenAI's no. 2 steps down from leading AGI work, reportedly due to illness.
tech.key_point: She held one of OpenAI's most senior operating roles, the departure lands the same week as the GPT-5.6 launch.
tech.for_you: No direct action, but worth watching OpenAI leadership churn if you're betting agency infrastructure heavily on their roadmap staying stable.

tech.name: OpenAI ChatGPT Atlas
tech.hook: OpenAI quietly kills its standalone AI browser after a short run.
tech.key_point: Atlas is being sunset just months after launch, a sign OpenAI is consolidating around ChatGPT Work instead of standalone apps.
tech.for_you: Confirms the pattern: OpenAI is folding features into ChatGPT rather than shipping separate apps, so build integrations against the core ChatGPT/API surface, not adjacent products that might get cut.

tech.name: SK Hynix
tech.hook: SK Hynix raises $26.5bn in the largest ever Nasdaq debut by a foreign firm.
tech.key_point: Comes amid a memory chip crisis already pushing sub-$400 smartphone sales down 22%.
tech.for_you: No direct action, but memory prices climbing could eventually push up compute/hardware costs relevant to any local-inference plans for clients.

tech.name: EU vs Meta
tech.hook: EU orders Meta to redesign Instagram and Facebook, calling them deliberately addictive.
tech.key_point: EU findings say the apps are engineered to 'shift the brain into autopilot mode.'
tech.for_you: If any yoga/meditation platform positioning leans on 'anti-addictive, mindful tech', this regulatory pressure on Meta is a useful contrast point in your marketing narrative.

tech.name: Microsoft Xbox
tech.hook: Microsoft's Xbox division cuts jobs as its Game Pass bundling strategy fails.
tech.key_point: Stratechery frames it as a broader lesson on bundling economics breaking down under sunk-cost pressure.
tech.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness.
